skill.name: aigcpanel-cli-skill
skill.description: 通过 AIGCPanel 内置 HTTP 接口或命令行 CLI 工具调用本地 AI 模型和任务处理能力。当需要列出可用模型、安装/删除模型、调用模型生成内容、查询任务结果、查看模型日志、设置模型参数、查看 ComfyUI 工作流、或批量处理视频/音频/图片时使用本技能。适用场景：自动化脚本调用 AI 模型、外部程序集成 AIGCPanel、批量处理任务、CLI 命令行调用。
skill.summary: Use AIGCPanel CLI commands and authenticated HTTP endpoints to manage local model services and run media tasks.
skill.author: modstart-lib

security_audit.summary: All 80 static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, readable multilingual text, or a local video-compression command. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or encoded payloads in the supplied guide. A separate low-severity issue affects unquoted versioned service identifiers, which Bash interprets as pipelines; the external application implementation was not supplied.

remediation.issue: Versioned service identifiers contain unquoted pipe characters in Bash examples.
remediation.suggestion: Quote every complete name|version argument in Bash examples, including model calls, settings, logs, and workflow listings.

semantic_findings.title: Unquoted service identifiers create unintended shell pipelines
semantic_findings.description: Examples such as '--server server-demo|1.1.0' leave the pipe unquoted. Bash launches the version token as a command and passes an incomplete identifier to AIGCPanel. This can invoke an unintended PATH executable instead of the requested model operation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples explicitly use Bash fences and unquoted pipe operators. Pipeline interpretation is certain; execution of an unintended executable depends on PATH contents.

content.user_title: Automate Local AI Tasks with AIGCPanel
content.value_statement: Managing local AI models and media tasks requires consistent commands and reliable result handling. This guide documents AIGCPanel CLI operations and authenticated HTTP workflows.
actual_capabilities: Documents model service listing, local installation, removal, log inspection, and settings updates.
Explains model calls for speech synthesis, transcription, image generation, video generation, and ComfyUI workflows.
Provides built-in tool examples for video compression, resizing, merging, subtitles, and audio processing.
Explains JSON arguments and parameter-file options for complex inputs.
Documents authenticated HTTP task submission, status polling, result retrieval, and error handling.
Describes configuration and render-confirmation stages for paused media tasks.
limitations: Contains documentation only; AIGCPanel, its CLI, models, and media-processing tools must be available separately.
Available functions depend on installed services and workflows; the guide does not verify model quality or runtime behavior.
ComfyUI workflow listing requires VIP access; non-VIP users receive an empty list.
Some Bash examples omit required quoting around versioned service identifiers; model settings also require a service restart.

use_cases.title: Integrate local model services
use_cases.description: Connect an application to authenticated HTTP endpoints, select an installed model, submit tasks, and retrieve completed results.

use_cases.title: Prepare media-processing batches
use_cases.description: Use documented tool commands to plan repeatable video compression, audio normalization, subtitle insertion, and format conversion.

use_cases.title: Maintain model services
use_cases.description: Inspect installed services and logs, update GPU or idle-timeout settings, and manage approved local model installations.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect installed services
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the AIGCPanel guide to list installed model services and summarize available functions. Do not install, remove, or change anything.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a media tool call
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an AIGCPanel VideoCompress invocation for [video path]. Explain expected result handling, quote shell arguments safely, and wait for approval before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Select a ComfyUI workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect workflows for [service identifier], verify VIP availability, and prepare a call using [workflow name] and [parameter file]. Quote the complete service identifier.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: workflow discovery and complex parameters

prompt_templates.title: Design an HTTP task integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an authenticated AIGCPanel HTTP integration for [function]. Include service discovery, bounded polling, error handling, and result extraction. Keep bearer tokens out of output.

output_examples.input: Summarize the sample installed-service response in the guide.
output_examples.output: The sample lists server-ComfyUI version 1.0.0. Select a function reported by your installed service before submitting a task.

output_examples.input: Explain how an HTTP client should handle task responses.
output: Store the task identifier returned when the model call is accepted.
Poll the query endpoint while the task remains pending, using the documented 500-millisecond interval and a client timeout.
On success, extract the returned result and output path. On error, report the task error without exposing authentication details.

output_examples.input: The workflow list is empty. What does the guide say?
output_examples.output: Workflow listing requires VIP access, and non-VIP users receive an empty list. Check access and the selected service before assuming workflows are missing.

best_practices: List installed services first, select the intended version, and quote complete service identifiers containing pipe characters.
Keep bearer tokens private and use them only with the intended AIGCPanel application endpoint.
Confirm model removal and task continuation with the user, and apply timeouts when polling long-running tasks.
anti_patterns: Copying versioned service identifiers into a shell without quoting the pipe character.
Sharing the authentication file, bearer token, or sensitive model logs in public output.
Assuming every listed function exists locally or that model settings take effect without restarting the service.

faq.question: Does this skill include AIGCPanel or AI models?
faq.answer: No. It contains an integration guide. Install AIGCPanel and the required model services separately.

faq.question: How do I install the CLI?
faq.answer: Open AIGCPanel settings, select CLI tools, and choose the system installation option. The guide also names a local CLI build command.

faq.question: How are HTTP requests authenticated?
faq.answer: Read the port and token from the application userData authentication file. Include the token in the Authorization bearer header.

faq.question: Can I omit the model service version?
faq.answer: Yes, when the name matches exactly one installed version. Multiple matches require an explicit version; quote versioned identifiers in shell commands.

faq.question: Why does ComfyUI workflow listing return nothing?
faq.answer: Workflow listing requires VIP access. The guide states that non-VIP users receive an empty list.

faq.question: How do I handle tasks that need confirmation?
faq.answer: Use the returned task identifier to resume the required configuration stage. Some tasks also require a separate render-confirmation stage.
